originalTitle: Fed's Warsh vows to 'do my job' if challenged by Trump
simplifiedContent: The head of the Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh, said he will do his job and make decisions about interest rates without being influenced by President Trump. This is important because the Federal Reserve is supposed to be independent and make decisions based on what's best for the economy, not based on politics. Warsh also said that he will keep working to control inflation, which is when prices for goods and services rise too quickly. Even though inflation went down a bit in June, Warsh doesn't think the Fed should lower interest rates right now. The markets are watching Warsh's decisions closely, and his statement made them think that interest rates might not go up as quickly as they thought.

originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Wednesday
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the Indian stock market went down because of rising tensions in West Asia, which made oil prices go up and the value of the Indian rupee go down. This is a concern because it could lead to higher prices for goods and services, which is called inflation. The main stock market indexes, Sensex and Nifty, fell by up to 0.7%. This happened even though some investors were feeling optimistic about company earnings, but the worries about global tensions were stronger. Overall, this means that investors are nervous about what might happen next in the market.

originalTitle: Goldman Sachs profit tops estimates on trading boom, corporate deal spree
simplifiedContent: Goldman Sachs, a big financial company, just released its quarterly earnings report and it's better than expected. The company made a lot of money from trading and helping other companies make big deals, which led to a big increase in its profits. This is good news for the company and its investors, which is why its stock price went up after the report came out. The company's wealth management business also did well, which helped add to its overall strong performance. This matters because it shows that Goldman Sachs is doing well and making money in different areas of its business.

originalTitle: Gold, silver prices today: Comex gold and silver rebound as softer US inflation eases Fed rate hike fears
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: gold and silver prices went up on July 14th because inflation in the US wasn't as high as expected. This makes investors less worried that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates. As a result, gold and silver prices increased, with gold reaching $4,112 and silver reaching $60. This change in prices matters because it shows that investors are feeling more confident about precious metals, at least for now. The softer inflation and other global events, like rising Middle East tensions, are supporting the increase in gold and silver prices.

originalTitle: Govt reviews fresh bids for IDBI Bank as stake sale process gathers pace
simplifiedContent: The Indian government and LIC (Life Insurance Corporation) are moving forward with selling a significant portion of their ownership in IDBI Bank. They plan to sell a combined 60.72% of the bank's shares, which includes 30.48% owned by the government and 30.24% owned by LIC. This sale also means that the buyer will get control over how the bank is managed. The government and LIC currently own almost 95% of the bank, so this sale is a big deal. This matters because it could lead to changes in how IDBI Bank operates and who gets to make important decisions about the bank's future.

originalTitle: Alpine Texworld IPO off to a slow start; subscribed 0.28 times on Day 1; GMP indicates modest listing
simplifiedContent: Alpine Texworld's initial public offering (IPO) got off to a slow start, with investors showing limited interest on the first day. This means that the company didn't receive as many bids as it had hoped for, except from a group of institutional investors who bought all the shares available to them. The company is trying to raise ₹126 crore to grow its business in Ahmedabad and pay off its debts. A slow start to the IPO might indicate that the company's stock price won't be very high when it starts trading. This could be a sign that the company's stock may not be very popular or valuable when it lists on the market.
